## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Goṇapetavatthu* ("The Ox", Pv 8) is a verse narrative in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Centering on the theme of consoling those overwhelmed by bereavement, the text addresses how one can help individuals stricken with grief [SuttaCentral]. In modern scholarship, B. C. Law mentions the story of the *Gonapeta* among various ghost accounts explored in his monograph *The Buddhist Conception of Spirits* [Law 1926].
SuttaCentral links the text thematically to several other Pali narratives concerning the pacification of grief, notably the *Sujātajātaka* (Ja 352), *Kaṇhapetavatthu* (Pv 18), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17), *Ubbaripetavatthu* (Pv 25), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83), *Migapotakajātaka* (Ja 372), *Somadattajātaka* (Ja 410), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449), and *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 454) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus confirms substantial Pali-internal text reuse between the verses of Pv 8 (§4–8) and these shared grief narratives, showing close alignment with the *Sujātajātaka*, *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka*, *Kaṇhapetavatthu*, *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka*, *Migapotakajātaka*, and *Somadattajātaka*, as well as their commentaries in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels are recorded in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
